summary: Today’s pulse tracks Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says, Half of NHS trusts in England lack funds earmarked to cover maternity leave, and Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven. Across BBC, Guardian, and NPR, the strongest repeated signals are england, south, and according. In the background, Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim and No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says
headlines.description: Further details have emerged about two police officers hailed for preventing a Polish gunman from killing more.

headlines.title: Half of NHS trusts in England lack funds earmarked to cover maternity leave
headlines.description: Physiotherapy services hit particularly hard compared with other areas of healthcare such as nursing Almost half of the NHS trusts in England have no earmarked funding to cover staff on maternity leave, according to analysis that raises fresh concerns about pressure on physiotherapy services. Freedom of information requests sent to the trusts across by the Chartered Society of Physiotherapy (CSP) found that 49% had neither a dedicated budget nor a policy to permit overspending to pay for maternity cover.

headlines.title: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
headlines.description: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 30 miles from Cairo At least seven people were killed and more than 100 others injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of Cairo, authorities have said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 30 miles (50km) south of the capital, when a train travelling to the south-western Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. It said one of the trains had derailed.

headlines.title: Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim
headlines.description: Bailiffs reportedly seized digital records before court case over alleged intellectual property breaches on Land Rover Defender Bailiffs acting for Jaguar Land Rover raided the Dutch offices of a Chinese “copycat” rival before a legal showdown this week over whether its “Defender clone” infringes intellectual property rights. Bailiffs acting on behalf of JLR reportedly seized digital records from the offices of Chinese carmaker BYD in Schiedam and Hoofddorp in August, according to the Sunday Times.

headlines.title: No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks
headlines.description: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, who will lead a caretaker government while negotiations take place, said: "I think everyone's over politics so let's all have a bit of a break for the next three weeks".

headlines.title: Met Office issues weather warning as UK conditions create ‘perfect recipe’ for fog
headlines.description: Travel may be disrupted until Monday morning in areas including most of southern England and across Midlands The Met Office has said weather conditions in the UK are creating a “perfect recipe” for fog as it warned that travel may be disrupted. A yellow weather warning lasting from 6pm on Sunday until 11am on Monday has been issued by the service, with the affected areas including most of southern England, excluding the south-west, and the entirety of the Midlands.

headlinePool.title: After a successful trip to Uruguay, Pope Leo heads to Argentina
headlinePool.description: On Sunday, tens of thousands packed the main square in Florida, Uruguay, to watch Pope Leo speak.

headlinePool.title: Footage shows derailed carriages after fatal train crash in Egypt
headlinePool.description: It is yet unclear what caused the accident but Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said an investigation is underway and will "hold accountable anyone who proves their negligence".

headlinePool.title: ‘No matter what, he doesn’t quit’: disabled wrestlers draw strength from ring alter egos
headlinePool.description: Scheme in Derry aims to sow confidence by getting people with learning and physical disabilities into wrestling The music thumped, the lights blazed and from the ring the announcer did a countdown. “Who is ready to rumble?” he roared. The bellows and cheers indicated that the crowd at St Columb’s Hall in Derry on Saturday night was more than ready for the Foyle Rumble, and so began a wrestling extravaganza of heroes and villains in leotards, masks and kneepads. The blend of athleticism and scripted storytelling would have been familiar to fans of WrestleMania, but this Northern Irish version came with a twist: many of the performers have learning or physical disabilities, and the characters they play in the ring do not quite stay in the ring.

headlinePool.title: Russell Brand to learn sentence after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault
headlinePool.description: Comedian Brand faces a "significant" prison sentence, which a London court judge is set to hand down on Monday.

headlinePool.title: Beef industry quietly squashes part of its own science curriculum after ranchers protest
headlinePool.description: Lesson for teenagers included how cattle’s methane emissions contribute to climate crisis, but it was then scrapped A beef industry-funded effort to teach teenagers about cattle’s climate impact was quietly scrapped following backlash from some ranchers, who disputed the premise that cows contribute to global heating. The episode is the latest example of the livestock industry’s decades-long battle to determine what US children learn about cows and the climate.

headlinePool.title: End of the ‘vomit comet’: Scillonian III sets sail on final voyage from Isles of Scilly
headlinePool.description: Much-loved passenger ship has traversed Atlantic swells between islands and Cornish mainland for almost 50 years Tears were shed, sea shanties sung and tales of stormy voyages exchanged as one of the UK’s most characterful ships set sail for the final time. Scillonian III, also known as the “vomit comet” because in stormy weather it tended to rock a little too much for the comfort of those susceptible to sea sickness, has chugged between the British mainland and the Isles of Scilly, for just shy of half a century.

headlinePool.title: Two police officers hailed as heroes for confronting Kraków gunman
headlinePool.description: Jakub Kulik critically injured and Artur Morański also wounded after actions that ‘prevented further casualties’ Two Polish police officers who were injured as they pursued and detained the gunman in Kraków on Saturday have been hailed as heroes. One of them is Jakub Kulik, a former paratrooper and volunteer firefighter, who was left critically injured after a close-range exchange of fire with the suspect, a 24-year-old Polish national who killed six and injured 17 in an attack believed to have been inspired by far-right ideologies.

headlinePool.title: Homes and temples glow across India to mark Diwali
headlinePool.description: Millions of Indians are marking the festival of lights with glowing lamps, fireworks and traditional sweets.

headlinePool.title: Israel’s president picks Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot to form government
headlinePool.description: Knesset has been deadlocked since the election last month when Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition lost its majority Israel’s president has ⁠chosen Gadi Eisenkot, the prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s ⁠strongest rival, to ⁠try to ​form a new government, after a deadlocked election that left neither man ⁠with a clear path to power. Isaac Herzog’s office said he had informed Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party, on Saturday night “of his intention to task him with forming a government”.
